clue.text: Ought to run after firstly enraging bear

indicators.note: after places the run abbreviation behind the letter taken from enraging

parts.note: ought to do something is should do it

indicators.note: firstly asks for just the opening letter of the word enraging

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A warning that someone must flee once a bear has been provoked.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to carry or endure it, which is one sense of bear as a verb.

clue.text: American's upset with bank? Without doubt

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the abbreviation for American upside down, reading it upwards

parts.note: US is short for American
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: An American annoyed with their bank declares something certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Surely is an adverb of certainty, a synonym for assuredly.

clue.text: Publicly exposing Sally

explanation.definitionFit: Outing is revealing someone's secret, especially sexuality, in public; it is also a sally, an excursion or trip.

clue.text: Where you might see cricketers play big shots

definitions.text: Where you might see cricketers play

explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the famous London cricket ground; big shots are important people, peers or lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord's is a London venue for cricket matches, and lords are powerful nobles, informally big shots.

clue.text: Stylish European student, for example, with a set of books

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, a student
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A fashionable young European scholar carrying a stack of volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in appearance, a synonym for stylish.

clue.text: Was useful to listen to enthralling record

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one word is held inside the other

parts.note: to heed is to listen to and take notice
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Someone finds it handy to hear a gripping album.
explanation.definitionFit: Helped is the past tense of aid, being of use.

clue.text: Feeling of joy surrounding electric vehicle's height

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for joy goes round the vehicle abbreviation

parts.note: elation is a feeling of great happiness
EV abbreviates electric vehicle

explanation.surface: Delight at the tall stature of a new electric car.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation is height above sea level or a reference point, a synonym for altitude.

clue.text: Job options I abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned, in the sense of wild and uninhibited, tells us to throw the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone dropping their alternatives about which work to take.
explanation.definitionFit: A position is a post or situation of employment.

clue.text: Fragile priest about to be embraced by girlfriend?

indicators.note: to be embraced by means held within the girlfriend's word

parts.note: a date is a romantic partner, here a girlfriend
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword favourite
c is circa, about

explanation.surface: A frail clergyman about to be hugged by his partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate means easily broken or damaged, a synonym for frail.

clue.text: Dentures almost shifted after king replied

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the king abbreviation

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: shifted means the letters are moved around into a new order
almost tells us to drop the last letter of the word dentures

explanation.surface: False teeth slipped after the monarch gave his response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims Dentures to DENTURE; 'shifted' rearranges that to ETURNED, which follows R.
explanation.definitionFit: Returned can mean answered or said in response, a synonym for retorted.

clue.text: Container ship circled by fish after third of waves

indicators.note: after places the boxed ship behind the letter from waves
third of asks for the letter in third place in the word waves
circled by means the fish's letters go around the ship abbreviation

parts.note: the eel is a long snakelike fish
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A boat surrounded by fish beyond the third wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is a hollow receptacle such as a bowl or jug, and also a ship.

clue.text: Wipe a large boxing ring

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the run of letters is held within the phrase

explanation.surface: Cleaning a large boxing ring with a cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a ringing of bells, so to peal is to ring.

clue.text: Painting gets Trump irate in the end

parts.note: lands as in secures or obtains, lands a job
to cap something is to outdo or trump it

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word irate

explanation.surface: A political swipe: a picture leaves Donald Trump furious in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a picture depicting a stretch of countryside.

clue.text: Greek deficit target's partly rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters found are read in reverse
partly means only some of the letters of these words are used

explanation.surface: Greece's goal for reducing its budget gap has been partly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes CITTA from 'defiCIT TArget's'; 'rejected' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic relates to Attica and Athens, so it means Greek, especially of the classical Athenian dialect.

clue.text: Heads of government ignored for the present

indicators.note: heads of means the opening letters of each following word

explanation.surface: Leaders of government brushed aside for now.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is something given, a synonym for present as a noun.

clue.text: Tree fern's uprooted after I get involved

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the letter I
uprooted means torn from its place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A gardener digs up a tree fern and then gets stuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprooted' rearranges TREEFERN into NTERFERE, placed after I.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere is to meddle or intervene in others' affairs.

clue.text: This could be lad I knocked unconscious

parts.note: the letters of lad I are those of laid put out of order, so the instruction ... would produce them

explanation.surface: A boy flattened by a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: LAID with OUT as an anagram signal gives 'lad I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid out means floored, flattened or knocked senseless.

clue.text: Questions from Charlie concerning exams

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
on means about or concerning
tests are examinations

explanation.surface: Queries from a student called Charlie about their exams.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest is to dispute or challenge, so contests is a synonym for questions as a verb.

clue.text: Guide is confused about son's mask

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters wrap the son abbreviation
confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is short for son

explanation.surface: A puzzled guide asks about a boy's disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' gives DISGUIE, and 'about' sets that around the S for son; 'mask' works as a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A disguise is a costume or covering to conceal identity, like a mask.

clue.text: Dropped old glove swapping note with daughter

indicators.note: swapping means one letter is replaced by another within the glove word

parts.note: a mitten is a kind of glove

explanation.surface: An old glove that has been mended with a different patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitted means left out, a synonym for dropped.

clue.text: Marlene perhaps shunning rich selection of food

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Marlene Dietrich was a German-American film star
the letters of rich are taken as written

explanation.surface: A film star avoiding rich food in her eating regime.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is the range of foods a person habitually eats.

clue.text: Downright offensive sort

explanation.definitionFit: Rank means utter, as in a rank amateur; foul-smelling or offensive; and a class or grade, a sort.

clue.text: Always upset outside church, I admit

indicators.note: outside means the reversed word goes around the church and I
in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, read upwards

parts.note: ever means always
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A churchgoer confesses to being constantly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EVER into REVE, which goes 'outside' CE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive guests is to let them in, to admit them.

clue.text: Metal inside of cage?

parts.note: the inside letters of cage are A and G, and Ag is the chemical symbol for a precious metal

explanation.surface: Bars made of some metal inside a cage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ag, from Latin argentum, is the chemical symbol for this precious white metal.

clue.text: Watch socialist hit the roof

parts.note: to watch is to see
red is slang for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: Watching a left-winger lose their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for becoming furious, like hitting the roof.

clue.text: Italian flower good for initially beautifying big cat

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Tiber flows through Rome

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of beautifying

explanation.surface: An Italian bloom good for decorating a large feline.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is a large striped wild cat of Asia.

clue.text: Lavish clubs in Essex I've redesigned

indicators.note: in means the clubs abbreviation is placed inside the rearranged letters
redesigned means reshaped into a new arrangement

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Extravagant nightclubs in the English county of Essex have been revamped.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county east of London. 'redesigned' makes EXESSIVE from ESSEX I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive means more than necessary, overdone like something lavish.

clue.text: Dismisses wind instrument, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means we want a word pronounced like the instrument

parts.note: the sax, short for saxophone, is a wind instrument

explanation.surface: Firing a woodwind player, judging by the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack an employee is to fire or dismiss them.

clue.text: Team's catching Leicestershire's opener in slips

indicators.note: catching means holding, so one letter is enclosed

parts.note: a side is a team; side's makes sides

indicators.note: opener refers to the first letter of Leicestershire

explanation.surface: A cricket side catches the Leicestershire opening batsman at slip.
explanation.walkthrough: Slips are fielding positions beside the wicketkeeper in cricket; Leicestershire is an English county side.
explanation.definitionFit: Slides and slips are both sudden losses of footing, synonyms as verbs or nouns.

clue.text: Find bird eating insect regularly by river

indicators.note: eating means the bird swallows the selected letters

parts.note: a dove is a bird

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word insect

explanation.surface: A bird finds an insect beside a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to come across or detect, a synonym for find.

clue.text: Edward's in stitches about vegetables

indicators.note: in means Edward's short form sits inside the reversed word
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to stitch is to sew
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward laughing hard about root crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in stitches' looks like a laughing fit, but 'stitches' is a verb; 'about' turns it back to front to give SWES, and 'in' places the short name inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedes are root vegetables, also called rutabagas.

clue.text: Made sure criminal's guarded

indicators.note: criminal means bad or crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook took care to be on guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured means careful and restrained, as in guarded words.
